Keith cars.

OK, here's the story. Japan speed limits are fucking ridiculously slow. Highway is between 80-100km. Most large roads max at 60km and inner city roads are about 30-40km/hr. Now the KEI is also referred to as a yellow number because the plates are broken into:

Yellow: 660cc class.yearly inspection which is a couple hundred. This is the only class that you don't have to register with the police for a parking sticker. You have to prove that you have parking for all other engine sizes and yes the police will come out and measure your parking space.

500 numbers are 1.5 to 2.6 or so, 2 year inspection almost $1000 for 2 years

300 numbers are 3l plus engine sizes, 2 year inspection which averages over $1500. Some parking lots charge more for these too.

800 numbers are modified 300 size suvs and such. Yearly inspection and will be a few hundred cheaper that a 300 number car. Laws have been tightening on this loop hole.

Now a KEI is cheap toaintaon and run. Taxes are like $80 a year compared to a Camry which will run about $400.

I mentioned speed limits. So a little KEI has no problem to drive all over Japan. Recently, they have actually gotten nicer since 2005. Older KEI cars were little sardine death traps ... They really did suck. Another to consider is that you don't have to drive much in Japan, public transportation in most suburb cases is good enough to commute. So, a house wives if they owned a car would be a KEI. Because they are so light weight they perform rather well in winter too, you just have to be careful at the 80km speed because they will flip on Icey roads. But inner city, shit all happiness. Driving a KEI in winter has to really look out for is ruts that big trucks leave behind. The KEI wheel base is smaller compared to a normal car so if you get into a rut situation you could end up having your tires pop off. This isn't common but I've seen a few in my lifetime.

So, the KEI running costs are crazy cheap:

$80 for yearly tax, $300 for inspection, and you get almost 30km per liter (liter of gas runs about $1.30) and your car insurance is about $40 (a 2l would be about $70). This alone makes them a no brainier to have as a second car that is only driven a few hours a month.
